Class ChaosAgentBootstrap

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.bootstrap.ChaosAgentBootstrap
@Internal public final class ChaosAgentBootstrap extends Object
JVM agent entry point and runtime bootstrap for the chaos testing agent.

Agent attachment modes

  • Static attachment (premain(String, Instrumentation)): the agent is specified via -javaagent:chaos-agent.jar=<args> on the JVM command line. All Phase 1 and Phase 2 interception points are installed before application classes are loaded, giving the agent full access to JDK bootstrap and platform classes. This is the mode used in production and CI test runs.
  • Dynamic attachment (agentmain(String, Instrumentation)): the agent is attached to a running JVM via the Attach API (e.g. VirtualMachine.attach()). Phase 2 interception points (Socket, NIO, HTTP, ...) are rewritten via JVMTI class retransformation on already-loaded JDK classes, so the same chaos surface is available as in static attachment.
  • Test helper (installForLocalTests()): installs the agent into the current JVM using ByteBuddyAgent.install(), intended for use in unit/integration tests that run without -javaagent:.

Idempotency

initialize(String, Instrumentation, Map) claims the static INITIALIZATION slot with a compare-and-set before installing anything. If two threads race during startup (e.g., concurrent dynamic-attach calls), only one installs; the other waits for its outcome and returns the same runtime (or the same failure).

Post-initialization steps

After the runtime is created and instrumentation is installed, the bootstrap:

  • Registers a ChaosDiagnosticsMXBean with the platform MBean server under the object name com.macstab.chaos.jvm:type=ChaosDiagnostics.
  • Registers JFR integration if jdk.jfr.FlightRecorder is accessible on the running JVM (stripped JREs without the jdk.jfr module are silently skipped).
  • Loads and activates a startup ChaosPlan from the configured source (inline JSON, Base64, or file path), if one is present.

Thread safety

All public methods are thread-safe. The initialization CAS in initialize(String, Instrumentation, Map) ensures that at most one runtime is installed at a time, and current() only ever returns a runtime whose installation completed.

  • Method Details

    • premain

      public static void premain(@Nullable String agentArgs, Instrumentation instrumentation)
      Static agent entry point, called by the JVM when the agent is specified via -javaagent:chaos-agent.jar=<agentArgs>.

      This method is invoked by the JVM infrastructure before the application's main method, ensuring that all instrumentation is in place before any application class is loaded.

      Nothing here initialises java.util.logging: the application's main may still choose the LogManager (java.util.logging.manager, as WildFly and Quarkus do), and the first logger fixes it. The agent's log lines are held (AgentLog.hold()) and the platform MBean, whose server initialises the LogManager too, is not registered yet: an agent thread does both once the application has initialised java.util.logging, or after LoggingStart.LIMIT at the latest.

      Parameters:
      agentArgs - the raw argument string from the -javaagent command-line option, e.g. configFile=/etc/chaos/plan.json;debugDumpOnStart=true. May be null or blank if no arguments were provided.
      instrumentation - the Instrumentation instance provided by the JVM; used to install class-file transformers for all interception points

    • agentmain

      public static void agentmain(@Nullable String agentArgs, Instrumentation instrumentation)
      Dynamic agent entry point, called by the JVM when the agent is attached to an already-running JVM via the Attach API.

      Because application and JDK classes may already be loaded when this method is invoked, retransformation of previously loaded classes depends on whether the JVM supports it and whether the class-file transformer requests it. Interception points that require transforming bootstrap-loaded JDK classes may be ineffective if those classes were loaded before attachment.

      Security gate: dynamic attach requires an explicit opt-in via the ALLOW_DYNAMIC_ATTACH_PROPERTY system property or ALLOW_DYNAMIC_ATTACH_ENV environment variable. Without the opt-in, agentmain is a no-op and returns silently. Rationale: an attacker who can call the Attach API on a running JVM already has process-level code execution, but installing a chaos agent gives them the ability to rewrite bootstrap JDK classes, which is a strictly stronger primitive. Requiring an explicit opt-in prevents a chaos jar that happens to be on the classpath from being trivially weaponised by a lower-privilege attacker via VirtualMachine.attach.

      Parameters:
      agentArgs - the raw argument string passed to the attach call; may be null
      instrumentation - the Instrumentation instance provided by the JVM

    • installForLocalTests

      public static ChaosControlPlane installForLocalTests()
      Installs the chaos agent into the current JVM using ByteBuddyAgent.install(), without requiring the -javaagent: command-line flag.

      Used by the test extensions and by the framework integrations when chaos is enabled without -javaagent: on the command line. It performs a self-attach via the JVM Attach API and needs no JVM flag: where the JVM does not allow a process to attach to itself, ByteBuddy attaches from a helper process. On JDK 21 and later the JVM prints the JEP 451 warning for the dynamically loaded agent; -XX:+EnableDynamicAgentLoading or -javaagent: avoid it.

      If the agent is already installed, the existing ChaosControlPlane is returned immediately without reinitializing.

      Returns:
      the installed ChaosControlPlane; never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if dynamic self-attach is unavailable on this JVM (e.g., the jdk.attach module is missing, or the JVM runs with -XX:-EnableDynamicAgentLoading or -XX:+DisableAttachMechanism). In this case, run tests with -javaagent:chaos-agent.jar instead.

    • current

      public static ChaosControlPlane current()
      Returns the ChaosControlPlane for the currently installed chaos runtime.

      The control plane is available after any of premain(String, Instrumentation), agentmain(String, Instrumentation), or installForLocalTests() has completed successfully.

      Returns:
      the initialized ChaosControlPlane; never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the chaos agent has not yet been installed in this JVM
